executive.verdict: Prototype / reference implementation. Suitable as a delivery accelerator for a digital banking channel; not market-ready as a product.
executive.maturity: Concept / prototype (self-described tutorial 'concept', E-01). Happy-path API flows exist end-to-end; no UI, no production hardening.
headline: Money-movement rules are unsafe: negative amounts accepted, no ownership check, available balance double-adjusted, core ledger reachable via gateway (PDD-F-01..04).
Customer data is not scoped: every authenticated user can list all transfers and payments and read any account balance (PDD-F-05).
Functional breadth is narrow: 0 fully-implemented and 9 partial out of a 35-capability retail internet-banking reference list (PDD-G-01).
Regulatory capabilities (KYC/AML, SCA/MFA, consent, immutable audit) are absent (PDD-G-02).
Runtime configuration and container images depend on third-party-owned assets (PDD-R-01).
Business data (customers, revenue, adoption, KPIs, market position) is not in the repository and requires stakeholder validation.
executive.recommendation: Proceed only as an accelerator. Close Critical findings in a 4-6 week stabilisation phase before any external exposure; plan a 9-12 month programme to reach a bank-pilot MVP (indicative assessor estimate).

scorecard: Clean Feign seam to core, OIDC; no adapters (PDD-A-02)
MIT third-party code, branding, external deps (PDD-R-01, R-02)

vision: Not documented. README states an educational intent: an 'internet banking API concept' that evolves 'as a full fledged REST API collection until deployments'.
objectives: Implied by code: enable existing bank customers to self-onboard and perform transfers and bill payments online, separated from the core ledger.
value_proposition: Channel/core separation; modern Spring Cloud stack; standards-based identity (Keycloak/OIDC); one-command local environment with seed data and Postman collection.
segments: Not documented. Assessor inference: system integrators and bank IT teams seeking a greenfield digital-channel accelerator for smaller banks/credit unions/NBFCs. Requires stakeholder validation.
alignment: The implemented flows address the core of the stated problem (self-service money movement) but the absence of authorisation, validation and compliance features means the solution does not yet safely solve it.

features: No email/OTP verification, no password policy, password logged
No admin role; DISABLED/BLACKLIST do not disable Keycloak login
Ledger debit only; no biller settlement
Any account visible to any user
WebFlux UI starter in MVC services
business_value: Accelerator for a digital banking channel; demonstrates target architecture patterns.
Flows align with self-service outcomes (reduced branch transactions) but cannot be safely realised until Critical findings are fixed.
Self-registration with approval and straight-through intra-bank transfers would reduce manual work once secured; no ops tooling (reconciliation, admin console) yet.
Stateless services can scale horizontally; single-tenant design and simulated core limit commercial scaling.
Delivery-team productivity gain from reusable scaffolding; magnitude requires stakeholder measurement.

Password grant only; no MFA, no recovery
Works on happy path; unsafe rules, wrong balances, no confirmation/receipt
Ledger debit only; biller not paid

findings.title: Negative and zero amounts accepted for transfers and payments
findings.description: validateBalance only rejects when balance < amount; there is no amount > 0 rule and no Bean Validation. A negative transfer debits the beneficiary and credits the initiator.
findings.business_impact: Direct fraud/theft vector; customer funds can be moved without consent.
findings.recommendation: Enforce amount > 0 and max-amount rules at API and ledger level; add tests.

findings.title: No check that the customer owns the source account
findings.description: Orchestrators forward fromAccount/account verbatim to core; JWT identity is never mapped to the customer's accounts.
findings.business_impact: Any logged-in user can move money out of any account.
findings.recommendation: Introduce customer-account entitlement checks derived from the authenticated identity.

findings.title: Core ledger operations reachable directly by end users
findings.description: Gateway routes /banking-core/** to core-banking-service with only 'authenticated' required, bypassing channel services and their history records.
findings.business_impact: Unrecorded ledger manipulation; channel controls can be bypassed.
findings.recommendation: Remove public route to core; restrict core to internal service-to-service calls.

findings.title: Available balance shown to customers is wrong after every transaction
findings.description: After updating actualBalance, availableBalance is recomputed from the new actual and adjusted again (debit: -2x; credit: +2x). Any existing hold is overwritten.
findings.business_impact: Incorrect balances, wrongful declines/approvals, customer complaints, reconciliation breaks.
findings.recommendation: Correct balance arithmetic; model holds explicitly; add balance assertions in tests.

findings.title: History and lookups are not scoped to the customer
findings.description: Transfer and payment history use findAll(pageable); core account lookup returns any account by number.
findings.business_impact: Privacy breach exposing all customers' financial data.
findings.recommendation: Filter every read by the authenticated customer; restrict admin listing to back-office roles.

findings.title: Any authenticated user can approve or blacklist registrations
findings.description: PATCH /bank-users/update/{id} has no role check; Keycloak realm defines no business roles.
findings.business_impact: Self-approval / privilege escalation; onboarding control ineffective.
findings.recommendation: Introduce admin/ops roles and maker-checker approval.

findings.title: Blocked, dormant or pending accounts can transact
findings.description: AccountStatus enum exists but is never consulted during debit or credit.
findings.business_impact: Breach of account-freeze obligations (e.g. court orders, fraud holds).
findings.recommendation: Enforce status rules for both debit and credit legs.

findings.title: Failed payments remain PENDING/PROCESSING forever
findings.description: Orchestrators save a pending record, call core, then update to SUCCESS; exceptions are not handled and FAILED is never set; no reconciliation.
findings.business_impact: Phantom or duplicate payments visible to customers; operations cannot reconcile.
findings.recommendation: Explicit payment state machine with FAILED/REVERSED, timeouts and reconciliation.

findings.title: Duplicate submission creates duplicate debits
findings.description: No idempotency key; each POST creates a new transaction.
findings.business_impact: Double charging on client/network retries.
findings.recommendation: Idempotency-Key on payment APIs end-to-end.

findings.title: Utility payments debit the customer but no biller is paid
findings.description: Core utilPayment only debits the customer account; comment notes third-party biller API would be called; no settlement/suspense credit.
findings.business_impact: In a real deployment customer money would leave without settlement; prototype only.
findings.recommendation: Integrate a biller aggregator and post to a settlement account.

findings.title: Same-account transfers are permitted
findings.description: No from != to rule.
findings.business_impact: Noise in ledger; potential gaming of limits once added.
findings.recommendation: Reject identical source and destination.

findings.title: Disabling or blacklisting a user does not block login
findings.description: Only APPROVED triggers a Keycloak update; DISABLED/BLACKLIST only change the local status.
findings.business_impact: Blocked customers can still authenticate and transact.
findings.recommendation: Synchronise all lifecycle states to the IdP (disable user, revoke sessions).

findings.title: Clean separation between channel services and core ledger
findings.description: Channel services own requests/status; core owns balances and postings; integration via declarative Feign clients.
findings.business_impact: Positive: enables replacing the simulated core with a real CBS behind the same contract.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the boundary; formalise it as an anti-corruption/adapter layer.

findings.title: No adapter layer for real core banking, payment rails or billers
findings.description: Core is a simulated ledger; no interfaces for external CBS, interbank rails or biller aggregators.
findings.business_impact: Integration effort for first real deployment is unbounded until target systems are known.
findings.recommendation: Define CBS/payment-hub adapter contracts early (stakeholder input on target systems).

findings.title: API contracts are inconsistent across docs and code
findings.description: Postman uses /core/** and /payment/** and /bank-user while gateway routes are /banking-core/** and /utility-payment/** and controller uses /bank-users; account number typed Long in two services vs String in core.
findings.business_impact: Integrator friction; demos fail; latent data bugs for non-numeric account numbers.
findings.recommendation: Publish versioned OpenAPI specs as the contract; align Postman and DTO types.

findings.title: No customer-facing user interface
findings.description: Repository contains only backend services; interaction is via Postman/HTTP.
findings.business_impact: Cannot be piloted with customers without building web/mobile front-ends.
findings.recommendation: Build web (and later mobile) channel against the APIs.

findings.title: Error responses are technical and inconsistent
findings.description: Generic handler returns HTTP 400 with raw exception text for all unexpected errors.
findings.business_impact: Poor customer messaging; support cost; information disclosure.
findings.recommendation: Standard error model (RFC 7807) with user-safe messages and correct status codes.

findings.title: No customer dashboard or own-account listing
findings.description: No endpoint returns the authenticated customer's accounts.
findings.business_impact: Basic 'view my accounts' journey missing.
findings.recommendation: Add customer-scoped accounts query API.

findings.title: Accessibility cannot be assessed
findings.description: No UI exists; accessibility evidence not available.
findings.business_impact: Unknown; to be addressed once UI exists.
findings.recommendation: Adopt WCAG 2.1 AA as UI acceptance criterion.

findings.title: Configuration externalised but owned by a third party
findings.description: All runtime settings are pulled from JavatoDev-com config repo; changing behaviour requires editing a repo the organisation does not control.
findings.business_impact: Configurability exists but is not under the product owner's control.
findings.recommendation: Internalise configuration into an organisation-owned store.

findings.title: No multi-tenancy or multi-bank support
findings.description: Single realm, single schema set, no tenant identifiers.
findings.business_impact: Each bank deployment needs a separate stack; limits SaaS model.
findings.recommendation: Decide tenancy model with stakeholders before scaling commercially.

findings.title: Single-currency, single-product ledger model
findings.description: No currency field; account types enumerated but only savings used; transaction types limited to two.
findings.business_impact: Adding deposits, loans, FX or new payment types requires ledger redesign.
findings.recommendation: Generalise ledger model (currency, product, transaction codes).

findings.title: Accelerator value for digital-channel delivery
findings.description: Working skeleton of gateway, identity, discovery, config, tracing and three business flows reduces initial setup effort.
findings.business_impact: Positive: shortens time-to-first-demo for delivery teams.
findings.recommendation: Position as internal accelerator; quantify reuse savings with delivery teams.

findings.title: Business outcomes and KPIs not defined
findings.description: No documented KPIs, customers, revenue or SLAs.
findings.business_impact: Value case cannot be validated from the repository.
findings.recommendation: Obtain business case and KPIs from stakeholders.

findings.title: Narrow functional coverage versus a retail internet-banking reference set
findings.description: 0 fully-implemented, 9 partial, 26 absent of 35 reference capabilities (assessor checklist).
findings.business_impact: Large build effort before market parity.
findings.recommendation: Prioritised roadmap (see product-roadmap).

findings.title: Regulatory capabilities absent
findings.description: No KYC/AML, sanctions, SCA/MFA, consent, or regulator-grade audit trail.
findings.business_impact: Cannot be deployed in a regulated jurisdiction.
findings.recommendation: Compliance-by-design workstream; engage compliance early.

findings.title: Operational dependency on third-party assets
findings.description: Config repo and Docker images (javatodev/*) owned by original author.
findings.business_impact: Third party can alter or remove assets; supply-chain and continuity risk.
findings.recommendation: Fork and internalise config and image builds.

findings.title: No exclusive IP; rebranding required
findings.description: MIT-licensed third-party code; packages, realm, images and FUNDING.yml carry original branding.
findings.business_impact: Competitors can use the same base; limited acquisition value of code itself.
findings.recommendation: Retain licence notice; rebrand; value lies in additions.

findings.title: Low maintenance activity and single original author
findings.business_impact: Key-person and sustainability risk if upstream is relied on.
findings.recommendation: Own the codebase internally; build team knowledge.

findings.title: Seed test data shipped in production migration
findings.description: Flyway temp_data migration inserts sample customers and balances in every environment.
findings.business_impact: Fake customers/balances in production ledger.
findings.recommendation: Separate test data from production migrations.

findings.title: Published credentials in README and repository
findings.description: README publishes a test user password; compose and realm files contain secrets.
findings.business_impact: Any environment built from defaults is trivially accessible.
findings.recommendation: Rotate and externalise all credentials before any shared deployment.

strengths: Clear bounded contexts: onboarding/identity, transfers, bill-pay, ledger (PDD-A-01)
Modern, widely-skilled stack (Java 21, Spring Boot 3, Spring Cloud) (E-37)
Easy local setup with docker-compose, seed data and Postman (E-05, E-42)
Good learning documentation (tutorial series linked in README) (E-01)
weaknesses: Narrow functional scope; no UI (PDD-G-01, PDD-E-01)
Third-party-owned runtime assets and branding (PDD-R-01, PDD-R-02)
roadmap: Safe for internal demos; secrets rotated; config owned; rebranded; business case & KPIs obtained
MFA, dashboard, scoped history, beneficiaries, limits, idempotent payments, notifications, admin console, web UI
Real CBS adapter, interbank rail, biller aggregator, AML/fraud hooks, immutable audit, HA/DR, VAPT
Mobile, open banking, eKYC onboarding, tenancy model
limitations: Static analysis only - services were not executed end-to-end; findings marked Medium confidence (e.g. TDD-ARC-07) should be confirmed at runtime.
